title: termwork: one kitty process for every terminal, not one per terminal
description:
## .what

termwork launches one kitty PROCESS per terminal (`termwork.sh`, the per-terminal launch with
`allow_remote_control=socket-only` and its own `listen_on`). move to one kitty process that holds
every termwork window — `kitty --single-instance`, or one kitty driven by remote control.

## .why

measured on a laptop docked to a 4k monitor at 150%, where every frame is drawn by an Iris Xe iGPU:

- ~57 kitty processes live at once
- each one holds its own gpu context, glyph cache and repaint loop
- one process shares all three across every window

the load picture and the trials already settled live in `gotcha.a-docked-4k-monitor-taxes-the-igpu`
(desktop/system). this task is the "fewer kitty processes" lever it ranks third.

## .the shape of the fix

1. find what in termwork depends on one process per terminal — the per-window socket, the
   `listen_on` template, kill/stop by pid
2. pick the carrier: `--single-instance` with a shared socket, or `kitty @ launch --type=os-window`
   against one long-lived kitty
3. keep every termwork contract (`term.open/list/read/send/stop`) unchanged for callers
4. measure before and after: kitty process count, kitty rss sum, iGPU busy under the same workload

## .bounds

- ⚠️ one process is one blast radius: a kitty crash then takes every terminal with it. weigh that,
  and state the call
- never kill a live terminal or tmux to test this; prove it on fresh windows
- consider `repaint_delay` / `input_delay` in the kitty bundle as a separate, smaller lever
